scope: Bounded official evidence package for historical positive flood outcomes and current critical-reach context within ANA hydrologic unit 137754 (Cuenca Zaña), using Oyotún as a territorial reference rather than a basin clipping boundary.

sources.institution: Gobierno Regional de Lambayeque / Comité Regional de Defensa Civil

historical_positive_outcomes.date_reference: 2008-03-06 report; some described damage occurred in preceding days
outcome: Highland rainfall increased river flows across affected Lambayeque districts.
Río Nanchoc rise disrupted normal road and pedestrian movement between Nueva Arica and Oyotún.
Turbulent Río Zaña waters had swept away the improvised Las Delicias crossing, isolating Oyotún settlements and affecting agricultural commerce.
Río Zaña overflow caused approximately 200 hectares of rice and food crops to be lost.
Rainfall inundated critical sections of the Cayaltí-Oyotún road.

historical_positive_outcomes.source_text_note: The SENAMHI inventory visibly renders the river name as 'sña'; IRFEN preserves the source wording and treats it as the Oyotún flood-inventory row without silently correcting the text field.

official_geometry.note: The official ANA hydrologic unit is the research spatial unit. Oyotún is a territorial reference inside it, not the clipping boundary.

critical_reach_context.scope: ANA transmitted four reference technical sheets identifying critical points in the district of Oyotún.

critical_reach_context.proposed_intervention: cleaning/desilting and rock-armored dike on the right bank

scientific_limits: No event-day gauge rainfall or discharge is available in this evidence package for the 2008 or 2009 historical outcomes.
No confirmed negative control is inferred from absence of reports or from non-event years.
The 2008 regional report combines multiple affected districts and river reaches; it is not treated as a single synchronized basin hydrograph.
The 2009 SENAMHI row is a positive outcome record, not a calibrated hydrologic threshold.
ANA critical-point sheets and proposed works identify exposure and intervention needs; they are not observed inundation footprints, event-day hydraulic capacity measurements or IRFEN thresholds.
The current 2026 critical-reach state cannot be backcast as the channel condition of 2008 or 2009.
The official whole-basin polygon does not validate event-specific routing from Río Nanchoc or individual quebradas to each impact location.
accepted_research_uses: mechanism discovery for later hydrologic replay
forbidden_uses: district boundary substitution for hydrologic boundary
critical-point design values as observed event truth
current-channel condition backcast into historical events
